_comment: TEMPLATE for mcp.json, which is git-ignored because it holds API keys in
plain text. You normally do not copy this by hand: whichever starts first —
the app, or either server in mcp_server/ — copies this file to `mcp.json`
verbatim, once, if `mcp.json` is missing. After that `mcp.json` is what is
read, so editing THIS file changes nothing. Edit `mcp.json` instead, or use
Settings -> MCP servers.
You can also edit all of this from Settings -> MCP servers, which writes back
to that file in place. Editing by hand still works: press Reload afterwards.
Either shape is accepted, and whichever you write is the shape saved back:
{"servers": [ ... ]}        a list, as below
{"mcpServers": { ... }}     keyed by name, as most MCP clients write it
Unknown top-level keys (like this `_comment`) are preserved across a save.
Transport is Streamable HTTP only. There is no stdio support: this server is
itself already a local process, so it will not spawn children for you.
Each tool is exposed to the model as `<prefix>__<tool>`. Set `prefix` when two
servers expose the same tool name, otherwise the last one registered wins.
For a stdio-only server, bridge it yourself and point `url` at the bridge.
The reference filesystem server, for example:
npx -y mcp-proxy --port 8931 -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem C:/work
`self-reflection` is deepseekUI's own source, read-only. It is NOT started for
you: run `python mcp_server/self_reflection.py` first, then set `enabled` to true.
It exposes self__introspect, self__explain_file and self__read_source. Do not add
`allowedTools` there: that key is a filter, and anything unlisted is hidden.
An API key goes in `headers` as `x-api-key` — the Settings panel gives that one
header its own password field, and shows whether a server has one. It is sent
with every call, so the server can read it per request instead of at startup;
changing it needs no restart. It is stored here in plain text.
`mcp_server/mcpserver.py` (web_search + web_fetch) wants a free Gemini key there,
from aistudio.google.com/apikey — see the `websearch` entry below.
